note: Demand-signal sources for Washington, DC, researched 2026-11-18 (item 4 PR 2). Tenant DATA: registered by scripts/seed-demand-sources.ts through 0343's demand_source_register, never by a migration. Every source is 'unverified' until a MoO+ marks it. The NWS definition is not here: it lives beside its adapter (lib/demand-signals/nws-shared.ts). Terms quotes were read on checkedOn through a page-fetch tool: whoever marks a source verified re-reads the terms page first.

sources.name: NOAA NCEI observed weather (Access Data Service, CDO v2)
sources.gives: Observed daily temperature and precipitation: the actuals needed to score a weather signal (hindsight evidence only, E0).
sources.auth: Access Data Service: none stated. CDO v2: a free token.
sources.rateLimit: CDO v2: five requests per second and 10,000 requests per day per token.
sources.caveats: No terms sentence was read on an official page (the NCEI Open Data Policy is a PDF that was not read). Test queries for Reagan National returned an empty list, so the station and dataset parameters are unproven. PR 3 builds this adapter only after a person reads the policy.

sources.name: OPM federal operating status (DC area)
sources.gives: Open, delayed or closed status for federal offices in the DC area. A closure or delay removes much of the weekday lunch crowd.
sources.caveats: The API page carries no terms or licence statement. It is a weather and emergency dismissal status: it does NOT establish a government shutdown (a lapse in appropriations), which is entered by hand. With telework, Open does not mean people are downtown.

sources.name: OPM federal holidays calendar
sources.gives: Observed federal holiday dates through 2030, including the Friday or Monday a weekend holiday is observed on.
sources.caveats: No terms statement on the page. The app already computes federal holidays from the statute (5 U.S.C. 6103) with no feed; this calendar would only confirm observed days. One-off closures by executive order may be missing.

sources.name: U.S. Senate tentative legislative schedule
sources.gives: Days the Senate expects to be in session or in recess. Session days bring staff and visitors to Capitol Hill.
sources.termsQuote: Information presented on this site is considered public information and may be distributed or copied
conditions: Poll rarely (the schedule changes a few times a year).
The URL carries the year: a new definition is needed each January.
sources.caveats: Tentative and changes. Pro forma sessions are not real attendance.

sources.name: Congress.gov API (daily Congressional Record)
sources.gives: Days on which Congress actually held proceedings (after the fact).
sources.caveats: No licence statement was found on the API pages. It records the past, so it cannot be known at the decision.

sources.name: U.S. House legislative calendar
sources.gives: Days the House plans to be in session.
sources.caveats: PDF only; no terms read. A person enters recess weeks by hand.

sources.name: Federal Register API
sources.gives: Executive orders and notices, such as a one-off federal closure day.
sources.caveats: The documentation and legal pages redirected to an access-request page for automated clients, so the terms were not read. Not a shutdown signal.

sources.name: AlertDC (DC HSEMA)
sources.gives: Emergency, severe weather, utility outage and government closing alerts for DC.
sources.caveats: No public feed or API. A manager may subscribe and enter what matters by hand.

sources.name: WMATA developer API, GTFS and GTFS-realtime
sources.gives: Rail and bus incidents, advisories and elevator outages. A disruption changes commuter foot traffic near a station.
sources.auth: A free API key by registration.
sources.rateLimit: Not read on the official site (third-party documentation says 10 calls a second and 50,000 a day).
sources.termsQuote: revocable license to download, use, reproduce, and redistribute WMATA's Transit Data within your Application
conditions: Our own registered key (the public demo key is for limited testing only).
No sharing of the data outside the application's users; no WMATA marks or implied endorsement.
On termination every stored copy of WMATA data must be deleted: store derived facts only (a disruption on a date), never raw payloads in an append-only table.
Respect the call limits of the key's tier.
sources.caveats: The licence is revocable. Exact endpoint URLs sit behind the developer portal and were not read; a definition with the real endpoints is needed before an adapter is built.

sources.name: WMATA service advisory RSS feeds
sources.gives: Rail and bus advisories with no key.
sources.caveats: Whether the developer licence covers these public feeds is not stated anywhere that was read.

sources.name: Capital Bikeshare GBFS
sources.gives: Live bike and dock counts per station: a weak proxy for foot traffic near a shop.
sources.termsQuote: grants to you a non-exclusive, royalty-free, limited, perpetual license to access, reproduce
conditions: Internal use only: the data may not be hosted, published or sold as a stand-alone dataset.
No implied endorsement.
sources.caveats: Not a forward signal, and history exists only if we store snapshots. Low priority.

sources.name: Open Data DC: DDOT TOPS public space and occupancy permits
sources.gives: Permitted street and lane closures (construction, block parties, events) that block access near a shop.
sources.termsQuote: You can copy, modify, distribute, and perform the data, even for commercial purposes, all without asking permission.
conditions: Credit DDOT / Open Data DC where shown (requested, not required).
sources.caveats: DDOT warns that the US Park Police, Capitol Police, NPS and the Architect of the Capitol can close roads without it reaching this dataset. One catalogue lists the dataset as CC BY 4.0 rather than CC0; attribution satisfies both.

sources.name: DC government news feeds (Mayor, DDOT, MPD)
sources.gives: Press releases, including DDOT weekly traffic advisories and MPD special-event closures.
sources.termsQuote: content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 License
sources.caveats: The same page says the licence does not apply to District or state produced material, so it is ambiguous for these releases. Free text: a person or a later reviewed parser must turn an item into an event.

sources.name: MPD traffic advisories (special events, motorcades, demonstrations)
sources.gives: Narrative street closures for parades, races and demonstrations: closures the permit dataset misses.
sources.caveats: No feed. Times change between versions of one advisory. A manager enters the event by hand.

sources.name: Mayor's Special Events Task Group calendar (DC HSEMA)
sources.gives: The city's own list of permitted special events with date, hours and place: the best single forward list of street events.
sources.caveats: A PDF whose file name changes with every revision; it was not opened directly. Events on federal land may be missing.

sources.name: National Park Service API: events at the National Mall
sources.gives: NPS-run programmes at National Mall and Memorial Parks.
sources.termsQuote: a citation or acknowledgement of the National Park Service as the source is appreciated
conditions: Our own key.
Credit the National Park Service where shown.
Stay under 1,000 requests an hour.
sources.caveats: It lists ranger programmes, not the permitted demonstrations and festivals that move demand. Those are entered by hand.

sources.name: National Mall permitted demonstrations and festivals
sources.gives: Marches, rallies and festivals on the Mall (more than 4,000 permitted activities a year).
sources.caveats: No list or feed of permitted events was found. A manager enters large ones by hand.

sources.name: DC Public Schools calendar
sources.gives: School days, breaks and half days: family traffic and the availability of student staff.
sources.caveats: No terms specific to the calendar; the dc.gov terms are ambiguous for District material and the feed is hosted by Google. Event titles are free text: a person must say which mean no school.

sources.name: DC public charter school calendars
sources.gives: Each charter school's own academic calendar.
sources.caveats: One calendar per school and no citywide feed.

sources.name: George Washington University events calendar
sources.gives: Campus events near the Dupont / Foggy Bottom shop.
sources.caveats: Terms not read. About 1 MB of mostly small events: low signal without filtering.

sources.name: University academic calendars (GWU, Georgetown, Howard, American, Catholic)
sources.gives: Move-in, breaks, finals and commencement: about six dates a year per school.
sources.caveats: Web pages only. A manager enters the few dates that matter.

sources.name: MLB Stats API (Washington Nationals schedule)
sources.gives: The Nationals schedule with dates and venue.
sources.termsQuote: Only individual, non-commercial, non-bulk use of the Materials is permitted and any other use of the Materials is prohibited without prior written authorization from MLBAM.
sources.caveats: The quote is MLB's copyright notice (gdx.mlb.com/components/copyright.txt); the MLB terms of use also prohibit automated scripts. Home games are entered by hand (about 81 a season) from the team's downloadable schedule.

sources.name: Washington Nationals downloadable schedule
sources.gives: Home game dates and start times for the season.
sources.caveats: MLB's terms allow private, non-commercial use only: a person downloads it once a season and enters home games.

sources.name: NHL web API (Washington Capitals schedule)
sources.gives: The Capitals season schedule.
sources.termsQuote: only for non-commercial, informational, personal use
sources.caveats: Undocumented, and the NHL terms prohibit scraping and entering content into a database. Entered by hand.

sources.name: NBA schedule (Washington Wizards)
sources.format: HTML (the schedule JSON refused automated access)
sources.gives: Wizards home games at Capital One Arena.
sources.caveats: The NBA terms bar use in a commercial product or service. Entered by hand, or found through a ticketing source once one is verified.

sources.name: Washington Mystics schedule
sources.gives: Mystics home games.
sources.caveats: No feed found; terms not read.

sources.name: Washington Commanders schedule
sources.gives: Nine or ten home games a year (Landover).
sources.caveats: The NFL terms forbid commercial use and systematic retrieval. A manager enters the home dates.

sources.name: Audi Field events calendar (D.C. United and other events)
sources.gives: Every event at Audi Field: matches, concerts and others.
sources.caveats: The site publishes no terms of use (a privacy policy only). A published calendar feed, but nobody has confirmed we may store it. Do not scrape mlssoccer.com (its terms forbid it).

sources.name: Washington Spirit schedule
sources.gives: Spirit home matches at Audi Field.
sources.caveats: The site refused automated access; terms not read.

sources.name: ESPN site API (unofficial)
sources.gives: Schedules for every league from one undocumented endpoint.
sources.termsQuote: access, monitor, copy or extract the Disney Products using a robot, spider, script, or other automated means
sources.caveats: Undocumented, and its terms forbid automated access and commercial use.

sources.name: TheSportsDB (free tier)
sources.gives: Upcoming events per team or league.
sources.caveats: The terms page could not be read. The free key returns one result per call and home events only.

sources.name: BALLDONTLIE sports API (free tier)
sources.gives: Game schedules for MLB, NHL, NFL, WNBA and others.
sources.rateLimit: Free tier: 5 requests per minute, free endpoints only.
sources.termsQuote: You may use Data you lawfully obtain for any lawful personal or commercial purpose, subject to these Terms.
conditions: Our own key.
Stay inside 5 requests a minute.
Confirm which schedule endpoints the free tier includes before building an adapter (NBA needs a paid plan).
sources.caveats: Which schedule endpoints are free was not verified.

sources.name: Ticketmaster Discovery API
sources.gives: Events by venue and date for Capital One Arena, The Anthem, the 9:30 Club, Audi Field and Nationals Park (their tickets are sold through it).
sources.rateLimit: A default quota of 5000 API calls per day and 5 requests per second.
sources.termsQuote: Cache or store any Event Content other than for reasonable periods in order to provide the service you are providing.
conditions: Our own key, inside the daily quota.
No permanent archive of event content: keep only derived facts (date, venue, size class) and re-fetch.
Internal use only; nothing that replaces Ticketmaster.
sources.caveats: The quote is from the list of things a developer must NOT do. The caching clause conflicts with an append-only table of raw event content: an adapter must be designed around that before this is marked verified.

sources.name: SeatGeek Platform API
sources.gives: Events by venue, were its terms to allow it.
sources.caveats: The API terms and the developer portal could not be read. Refused until someone reads them.

sources.name: Eventbrite API
sources.gives: Public event search no longer exists.
sources.termsQuote: Access to this API was shut down at 11:59 pm PT on Thursday, December 12, 2019.
sources.caveats: There is nothing to collect.

sources.name: Bandsintown API
sources.gives: Concert dates per artist.
sources.caveats: Its help pages say each key is tied to one artist and the data is not meant for other uses without approval. The data terms could not be read.

sources.name: Capital One Arena event calendar
sources.gives: Games and concerts at the arena.
sources.caveats: No feed; terms not found.

sources.name: Nationals Park non-game events
sources.gives: Concerts and other events at the ballpark.
sources.caveats: MLB terms apply.

sources.name: The Anthem event calendar
sources.gives: Concerts at The Anthem (The Wharf).
sources.caveats: No feed and no published terms.

sources.name: 9:30 Club event calendar
sources.gives: Concerts at the 9:30 Club.
sources.caveats: A small room: probably a weak signal. No feed.

sources.name: Kennedy Center calendar
sources.gives: Performances at the Kennedy Center.
sources.caveats: The calendar and terms pages refused automated access.

sources.name: Smithsonian events
sources.gives: Museum events on and near the Mall.
sources.caveats: The events and terms pages refused automated access. Smithsonian Open Access covers collections, not events.

sources.name: Events DC (Walter E. Washington Convention Center and other venues)
sources.gives: Conventions and events at the Convention Center, which drive large lunch demand nearby.
sources.termsQuote: will not use any robot, spider, or other automatic device
sources.caveats: Automated collection is forbidden without written permission. A manager reads the public calendar and enters large conventions by hand.

sources.name: RunSignup race API
sources.gives: Races by state, city and date: road races close streets and bring crowds.
sources.rateLimit: No more than 2 concurrent API calls at a time.
sources.caveats: The page describes an open API licence but says content stays under the normal service agreements; the separate API Terms were not read. Only covers races registered there, virtual ones included.

sources.name: Running in the USA race listings
sources.gives: A broad list of local races.
sources.caveats: No API. Its robots file refuses automated reuse.

sources.name: Major annual races (Marine Corps Marathon, Cherry Blossom Ten Mile, Rock 'n' Roll DC)
sources.gives: The few races that close large parts of the city.
sources.caveats: A handful of dates a year: entered by hand.

sources.name: National Cherry Blossom Festival events calendar
sources.gives: Festival events (parade, kite festival, Petalpalooza) across three weeks each spring.
sources.caveats: A terms-of-use page exists and was not read.

sources.name: Capital Pride parade and festival
sources.gives: The June parade and festival, both near the Dupont shop.
sources.caveats: Two dates a year: entered by hand.

sources.name: GDELT Project news API
sources.gives: Searchable world news coverage: could surface a planned march, strike or closure.
sources.termsQuote: any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the GDELT Project and a link to this website
conditions: Cite the GDELT Project with a link wherever its data is shown.
At most one request every 5 seconds.
sources.caveats: Headlines are not events: turning coverage into a dated event needs a reviewed rule or a person. Automatic discovery from news is a later PR.

sources.name: Google News RSS search
sources.gives: Headlines for a search query.
sources.caveats: Undocumented. Google's terms forbid automated access against its machine-readable instructions, and the robots file for the feed was not read.

sources.name: WTOP news feed
sources.gives: Local news for the Washington area.
sources.termsQuote: The systematic retrieval of any of the Content to create or compile
sources.caveats: The quote is from a list of prohibited uses; the terms allow private, non-commercial use only. A person may read it.

sources.name: Washington Post local feed
sources.gives: Local news for the Washington area.
sources.caveats: The terms page refused automated access. Refused until someone reads it.

sources.name: PoPville neighbourhood feed
sources.gives: Neighbourhood news and street-level notices.
sources.caveats: Its robots file disallows AI crawlers and its terms were not read. A person may read it.

sources.name: Nager.Date public holiday API
sources.gives: Public holidays by country and year.
sources.termsQuote: For commercial purposes we require active sponsorship.
sources.caveats: Not free for a business, and not needed: federal holidays are computed in code.
